audit.why: TRICKY at 7/10 with 54.04% over 396 games — the difficulty is early-weighted, which the chart already reflects (Graves 1 through 4-5, Skill from 6 on). End of the Line at 925 and Smoke Screen at 950 outrange everything Sejuani owns before her ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-2/3 spike and whys[3] both talk about 'Quickdraw charges' plural and give no cooldown, so there is no window a player can actually count.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s, and Riot adds that 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown' — so the window is not fixed, it shrinks every time he lands an auto. That is the real spike behaviour and it changes the advice: deny him autos on you and the escape stays down. Glacial Prison at 1300 is genuinely longer than a Quickdraw dash, which is why level 6 flips the lane.
audit.corrected: Quickdraw's 16s and its auto-attack refund written into the cooldown block, whys and dosFull; the level-6 flip priced at 1300 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four problems. (a) 'your Permafrost passive resistances' and 'your Permafrost passive stacks' — the resistances are Frost Armor from Fury of the North. (b) 'the blizzard's second stun' — Glacial Prison stuns only the first champion hit; the storm slows everyone else. (c) 'one accurate comet' — it is a bola. (d) The single best piece of counterplay in this matchup is absent: New Destiny's bullets cannot pass through units.
audit.why: Riot on New Destiny: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.' A minion standing between you and Graves eats his entire auto — for a melee tank walking up a lane, that is the whole approach plan and it was never written down. Riot on Glacial Prison: 'freezes and stuns the first champion hit and creates an ice storm that slows other enemies' — one stun, then slows. Riot on Fury of the North: Frost Armor, out of combat, armour, MR and slow immunity.
audit.corrected: Minion-block written into whys[0] and early; the fabricated second stun removed; Frost Armor and bola named correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gives Quickdraw no number and describes it as having 'charges'.
audit.why: Quickdraw 16/15/14/13/12s (cooldown reduced by his basic attacks), End of the Line 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6s at 925, Smoke Screen 26/24/22/20/18s at 950 — his longest cooldown by a wide margin and the one that actually gates his kill pattern.
audit.corrected: Quickdraw's number and refund mechanic written in, with Smoke Screen's 26s named as the kill-pattern gate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions that End of the Line detonates on terrain.
audit.why: Riot: 'Graves fires an explosive shell that detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain.' Fighting with your back to a wall changes when his Q goes off, which matters a great deal to a melee champion who is usually the one hugging terrain to shorten an approach.
audit.corrected: Written into the early block as a reason not to approach along a wall.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly calls Smoke Screen a blind.
audit.why: Riot's description says only that it 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range' and slows on impact. Whether it also blinds basic attacks is not in the kit data and needsResearch is empty by design, so the page should describe the vision denial it can source and stop there.
audit.corrected: Reworded to sight-range denial in whys[2] and spikes[3]. Flagged as unverified rather than asserted either way.

edits.after: Neither has a combo at level 1 — Frost Armor rewards standing back, and New Destiny fires four bullets that cannot pass through units, so a minion in the way eats his damage.
edits.before: Neither has their combo at level 1 — your Permafrost passive resistances reward standing back, and his shotgun autos lose damage at max range, so both sides farm safely.

edits.after: Level 1 is a standoff — but New Destiny fires four bullets that cannot pass through units, so keep a minion between you and him and his autos land on the minion instead. Hug the back of the wave and farm with W's first arc from distance. At level 2 Graves has Q and Quickdraw; he will fire End of the Line into you, dash to reload, and repeat before you can respond. Do not approach along a wall — the shell detonates on contact with terrain as well as after a second, so terrain shortens his fuse, not yours. Level 3 is his real danger spike: Smoke Screen strips your sight, End of the Line goes off inside it, and Quickdraw is the exit — if you are low at 3, walk back rather than trading into a burst you cannot see coming.
edits.before: Level 1 is a standoff — his shotgun auto range threatens if you stand in the open, but your Permafrost passive grants bonus resists when untouched, so hug the back of the wave and farm with W's first strike from a distance. At level 2 Graves has his Q and a Quickdraw charge; he will look to fire End of the Line into you, dash to reload, and repeat before you can respond — stay behind your minions so the shell bounces wide and doesn't arc back into you. Level 3 is his real danger spike: Smoke Screen drops your vision, End of the Line detonates in the fog, and Quickdraw gives him the exit — if you're near low HP at 3 respect the all-in and walk back rather than trading into an unseen burst.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are the chess phase: Quickdraw's armour makes short trades clean for him, and every auto he lands on you refunds part of its 16-second cooldown, so denying him free autos is how you keep his exit down. One overaggressive step lets you chain Q-W-E and force a Flash or a kill with jungler follow-up — be patient and do not chase him past the wave. Level 6 is your hard flip: Glacial Prison travels 1300, further than Quickdraw dashes, and once the bola stuns him you Q in, land both W arcs for full Frost, and Permafrost. The storm slows everything else around him, so his exit is gone.
edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are the chess phase: his Quickdraw armor stacks make short trades clean for him, but your W second-strike Frost application means one overaggressive step lets you chain Q-W-E and force a flash or a kill with jungler follow-up — be patient and don't chase him past the wave. Level 6 is your hard flip: Glacial Prison travels far enough to catch him before Quickdraw's dash can clear the blizzard, and once he's rooted in the impact zone you Q in, W to apply full Frost, and E stun him before the blizzard's second stun even triggers — he simply cannot trade resources with that CC chain active.

edits.after: - Graves Quickdraw (16/15/14/13/12s): matchup-defining — his exit, and his own basic attacks refund part of it, so deny him free autos. - Smoke Screen is 26s at rank 1 and gates his kill pattern. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.before: - Graves Quickdraw: matchup-defining — Dash + armor stacks — burst him after the charges are spent. Check it before every step-up. - Q dash is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.

edits.after: Frost stacks decide every trade: fight only with the full Q-W-E chain up and Quickdraw's 16 seconds still running.
edits.before: Frost stacks decide every trade: fight only when the full Q-W-E chain is available. Track Quickdraw before stepping up.

edits.before: Track Graves’s Quickdraw: Dash + armor stacks — burst him after the charges are spent. It’s down or you don’t go.

notes: Best single addition here: Riot's New Destiny text says his four bullets 'cannot pass through units', so a minion body between Sejuani and Graves absorbs his basic attack outright. For a melee tank whose whole problem is walking 925 units into a shotgun, that is the approach plan, and it appeared nowhere on the page. Second addition: End of the Line 'detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain' — approaching along a wall shortens his fuse. Removed a fabricated mechanic: 'the blizzard's second stun' — Glacial Prison stuns only the first champion hit, everything else in the storm is slowed. UNVERIFIED and left alone rather than asserted: the page calls Smoke Screen a blind. Riot's description only says it reduces sight range and slows on impact; whether it blinds basic attacks is not answerable from the kit file, so the text now says sight range and the question is recorded rather than guessed.
